info.title: Telegram Ads API (reverse-engineered)
info.description:
Reverse-engineered OpenAPI spec for the **Telegram Ads** self-serve platform (https://ads.telegram.org) — the
dashboard for running promoted messages in Telegram broadcast channels, paid in **TON** (and **Telegram Stars**).

> Unofficial. Reconstructed from the public client (`telegram.org/js/promote.js`, `main-aj.js`) and live read-only
> probing of an authenticated account. No official API documentation exists.

## API Architecture
The dashboard is a server-rendered jQuery app on Telegram's lightweight **"Aj"** framework. It is **not** a REST API —
it is a single JSON-RPC-style dispatcher:

- **All actions:** `POST /api?hash={sessionHash}` with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body `=<params>&method=<methodName>`.
  Responses are JSON: `{"ok":true, ...}` on success or `{"error":"...", "field"?: "..."}` on failure. Some return
  `{"redirect_to"}`, a `{"confirm_text","confirm_hash"}` challenge, or `{"toast"}`. Logical errors still return HTTP 200;
  **HTTP 401** means the session expired.
- **File methods** (media upload, `createAudience`) use `multipart/form-data`.
- **Auth** uses two separate endpoints (`/auth/request`, `/auth/login`), not the dispatcher.

This spec models the real transport faithfully: see `POST /api` for the dispatcher (one `oneOf` body schema + example
per method) and the `x-rpc-methods` extension for a method→schema index. There are **53 RPC methods**.

## Authentication
Session **cookies** set after login: `stel_token`, `stel_ssid`, `stel_adowner` (mirrors the `owner_id`), `stel_dt`,
plus `.telegram.org` cookies `stel_acid`, `stel_ln`. Every `/api` call also needs the per-session **`hash`** query
parameter, read from the page's `ajInit({...,"apiUrl":"/api?hash=XXXX"})` state. Most methods are scoped to one ad
account via the `owner_id` parameter (the `ownerId` embedded in the account page state).

## E2E Flow: Log in
1. `POST /auth/request` `{phone}` → `{temp_session}` (Telegram sends a confirmation message to that account).
2. Poll `POST /auth/login` `{temp_session}` (~every 700 ms). Falsy while pending; truthy once the user taps confirm,
   which sets the session cookies.
3. Load any `/account*` page and read `apiUrl`/`ownerId` from the embedded `ajInit(...)` state. You now have the
   `hash` and `owner_id` for all `/api` calls.

## E2E Flow: Create an ad
1. **Resolve targeting** — `searchChannel` / `searchBot` / `searchTargetQuery` / `searchLocation` (and optionally
   `getSimilarChannels` / `getSimilarBots`) to turn usernames/phrases into opaque `val`/`id` tokens.
2. **(optional) Upload media** — `POST /file/upload` (target=`ad_media` or `promote_photo`) → media reference.
3. **Validate/preview** — `checkAdPost` with the draft content + targeting → recommended CPM, rendered preview, field errors.
4. **Create** — `createAd` with content, targeting (`target_type` + channels/bots/search_queries + filters), `cpm`,
   `budget`/`daily_budget`, optional schedule → `{ok:true, redirect_to}`. New ads start in **In Review**.
5. **Manage** — `getAdsList` to monitor; `editAdStatus` (start/stop), `editAdCPM`, `editAdDailyBudget`,
   `incrAdBudget` (add TON) / `incrStarsBudget` (add Stars), `editAd`, `deleteAd`.

## E2E Flow: Fund the account
`sendAddFundsRequest` (advertiser onboarding/budget application reviewed by Telegram). Between linked accounts:
`linkAccount`, then `getAccountsForTransfer` / `searchAccountForTransfer`, then `transferFunds` / `transferWithdrawFunds`
(may return a `{confirm_text,confirm_hash}` challenge to re-submit).

## Targeting model (createAd / editAd / checkAdPost)
| target_type | Primary field | Meaning |
|-------------|---------------|---------|
| `channels`  | `channels` (+ `exclude_channels`) | Show in / based on specific channels. Up to 100. |
| `bots`      | `bots` | Target bot / mini-app audiences. Up to 100. |
| `search`    | `search_queries` | Show against search queries. Up to 10. |

Cross-cutting filters: `countries` + `locations`, `audiences`, topic toggles (`exclude_politic`/`only_politic`,
`exclude_crypto`/`only_crypto`, `intersect_topics`), `device`, `placement`, `views_per_user` (1–4), `picture`.

## Limits & constants (from page state)
- Ad text: **160** chars (`textMaxLength`). • Channels/bots: **100** each. • Search queries: **10**.
- Photo upload ≤ **5 MB**; video ≤ **20 MB**. • Currency: **TON** (2 decimals); also **Telegram Stars**.

## Ad status values
`In Review` (observed), and commonly `Active`, `Stopped`, `Scheduled`, `Declined`, `Completed`.

## Examples and compatibility
All examples use fictional identifiers. This unofficial interface may change without notice.
Method availability depends on the account; response schemas are inferred from the public web client.

post.description:
Single JSON-over-form RPC endpoint behind the entire Telegram Ads dashboard.

**How to call any method:** POST `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (or `multipart/form-data` for file methods) with the method's parameters plus a `method` field naming the RPC method. Authentication is by session cookies, and the `hash` query parameter (read from the page's `ajInit({apiUrl})` state) is required.

**Response envelope:** JSON. Success is `{"ok":true, ...}` (method-specific extra fields); failure is `{"error":"..."}`, often with `{"field":"..."}`. Some methods return `{"redirect_to":"..."}`, a confirmation challenge `{"confirm_text","confirm_hash"}`, or `{"toast":"..."}`. HTTP status is 200 even for logical errors; an HTTP 401 means the session expired (client redirects to /auth).

The `requestBody` below uses `oneOf` across one schema per method; pick the matching method example from the examples dropdown. Each method also has a dedicated `<Method>Request` schema in components. See the top-level `x-rpc-methods` extension for a machine-readable index (method → request/response schema → side-effect).

post.description:
Uploads a photo/video for use in an ad. Returns a media reference passed back to createAd/editAd as `website_photo` (target=promote_photo) or `media` (target=ad_media).

Limits (from page state): photo ≤ 5,242,880 bytes (5 MB), video ≤ 20,971,520 bytes (20 MB).

Cookie-authenticated. multipart/form-data.

post.summary: Start phone login — request Telegram confirmation
post.description:
Step 1 of login. Sends a login confirmation message to the phone number's Telegram account and returns a `temp_session` to poll with /auth/login. No cookies required yet.

Body: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

Step 2 of login. Poll repeatedly (~every 700 ms) with the `temp_session` from /auth/request. Returns a falsy body while the user has not yet confirmed in Telegram; once confirmed it returns a truthy body and sets the session cookies (stel_token, stel_ssid, stel_adowner, …). After success, reload and read `apiUrl` from the page state to obtain the `hash` for /api calls.

Body: `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

200.description: Truthy when confirmed (cookies set); falsy/empty while pending.

title.description: Internal ad name (organizational only, not shown to users).

text.description: Ad message body. Max 160 characters (see `textMaxLength`). Telegram entities/emoji allowed.
text.example: Follow our channel for project updates.

button.description: Call-to-action button label / action key (e.g. the join/open action shown on the ad).

promote_url.description: The t.me link or Telegram resource the ad promotes (channel, bot, post, or web URL).

website_name.description: Display name for an external website ad (when promoting a non-Telegram URL).

media.description: Media reference for the ad image/video, as returned by POST /file/upload (target=ad_media).

ad_info.description: Optional advertiser info / disclosure text attached to the ad.

views_per_user.description: Max times the ad may be shown to the same user (1-4).

target_type.description: Targeting mode. `channels` = show in/based on specific channels; `bots` = mini-app/bot audiences; `search` = show against search queries.

placement.description: Where the ad is placed (e.g. in-channel feed vs. search results). Server-validated; tied to target_type.

device.description: Device/platform targeting selector (e.g. all devices, or a specific Telegram client platform).

channels.description: Semicolon-separated channel identifiers (vals from searchChannel) to target. Up to 100. Used when target_type=channels.

exclude_channels.description: Semicolon-separated channel vals to EXCLUDE (paired field of `channels`).

bots.description: Semicolon-separated bot identifiers (vals from searchBot) to target. Up to 100. Used when target_type=bots.

search_queries.description: Semicolon-separated search-query ids (from searchTargetQuery). Up to 10. Used when target_type=search.

countries.description: Semicolon-separated country codes to target by location.

locations.description: Semicolon-separated location ids (from searchLocation), scoped by chosen countries.

audiences.description: Semicolon-separated audience ids to target (from updateAudiencesState).

picture.description: Set to 1 to enable showing a picture/media with the ad.

intersect_topics.description: Set to 1 to require users match the intersection (AND) of selected topics rather than union.

exclude_politic.description: Set to 1 to exclude channels classified as political.

only_politic.description: Set to 1 to target ONLY political channels.

exclude_crypto.description: Set to 1 to exclude channels classified as crypto.

only_crypto.description: Set to 1 to target ONLY crypto channels.

cpm.description: Cost-per-1000-views bid, in the account currency (TON). Drives delivery priority.

budget.description: Total lifetime budget for the ad, in TON.

daily_budget.description: Optional daily spend cap, in TON.

use_schedule.description: 1 to enable an hourly delivery schedule (then provide `schedule`).

schedule.description: Hourly schedule bitmap/string (built by the schedule picker) when use_schedule=1.

schedule_tz_custom.description: Custom timezone offset for the schedule, when not using a named tz.
